title: Architect discussion
summary: A concrete proposal with separable decisions and evidence to collect.

sections.label: Adaptable proposal
sections.text: Choose one outcome and compare the current approach with a bounded alternative. Identify the people and systems involved, the acceptance evidence, operating limits and unresolved decisions. Use the findings to decide what to implement or test next.

sections.label: Workplace example
sections.text: The original proposal considered requirements and debt investigation, verified implementation and source-backed country-data review. These are separable opportunities, not a required three-workflow programme.

sections.label: Decisions to resolve
items: Choose one end-to-end capability and task owner for the baseline.
Confirm available clients, models, integrations, and execution environment.
Agree on required evidence, review ownership, and acceptance criteria.
Define applicable data, source and publication boundaries. A domain curation process may require candidate isolation and source-scope rules.
Select the smallest orchestration that satisfies recovery and state needs.

sections.label: Reviewable next result
sections.text: A capability map, sample evidence packet, evaluation cases, and measured small pilot that informs the next scope decision.

sections.label: Gap review: workflow use and checks
items: Recommended use: Frame a bounded proposal, compare alternatives and produce a decision package.
Show the current approach and at least one feasible alternative against the same acceptance evidence.
Name the decision owner and identify assumptions that need an experiment.
Workflow placement and checks are Atlas recommendations. Existing examples, tenant availability, older product claims and comparative benefits were not revalidated by this mapping review.

sections.label: Gap review: verified source contribution
sections.text: GOV.UK discovery guidance connects problem definition, constraints and success measures to the decision about a next phase. This scoped source fact was checked on 15 October 2026. The guide's broader workflow and examples remain Atlas proposals, not demonstrated outcomes.

catalog.applicability: Use when preparing a proposal for an architect or decision owner that compares the current approach with one bounded alternative. It lists the decisions to resolve, such as task owner, available clients and models, acceptance evidence and data boundaries, before a small measured pilot.
catalog.limits: Reading a topic does not configure tools, execute a workflow or establish passing evidence.
